html:
Hun Sen was prime minister of Cambodia from 1985 to 2023, one of the longest serving heads of government in the world. A former Khmer Rouge commander, he defected to Vietnam in 1977.

He rose in the government Vietnam set up after the 1979 invasion. After the 1993 election he shared power, then seized full control in fighting in 1997.

His rule brought peace, fast growth in garment making and tourism, and close ties with China, along with land grabs and the crushing of the opposition. In 2023 he handed the office to his son Hun Manet. See Norodom Sihanouk.
